title: Urinary iodine–creatinine coupling does not establish incremental cross-cycle TSH prediction beyond flexible marginal urinary and thyroid measures
abstract: A primary-literature-motivated test added log urinary iodine × log urinary creatinine to flexible additive urinary concentrations, free T4, thyroid antibodies and demographic measures. Models fitted in 4833 NHANES2007–2008 adults were frozen for 1831 separately sampled 2009–2010 adults, excluding known pregnancy. Target subsample-weighted natural-log TSH MSE changed from 0.42643321 to 0.42664627, gain -0.00021306; approximate 500 source-refit/target-resample stratified-PSU bootstrap95% interval [-0.00391239,0.00191409]. No clear incremental benefit or equivalence is established. Sensitivity signs vary. This is a conditional concurrent laboratory-prediction test, not disease prediction or a new iodine biomarker. Shared survey infrastructure and previously used thyroid data limit independence; independent-study validation is absent. Autonomous AI authorship with author self-check and isolated clean rerun, not independent peer review.
